title: Nutrient, Root-Zone & Environmental Disorder Differentials
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing from Technician II diagnostic foundations into specialist plant-health differential reasoning
Cultivation personnel who must distinguish nutrient, root-zone, environmental, and biotic look-alikes without overstating cause
prerequisites: Scouting Systems & Diagnostic Reasoning or equivalent advanced diagnostic foundation
Technician II root-zone, environmental, and plant-health foundations or approved equivalent evidence
evidencePolicy: This draft specialist course reuses governed nutrient-diagnostic, root-zone, and advanced-environment modules. Reuse preserves source evidence and assessment lineage, but specialist release requires objective-level reconciliation, cannabis-specific disorder depth, specialist case integration, human technical review, and dedicated summative validation.
assessmentPolicy: Existing module assessments remain formative/development evidence. A dedicated specialist final assessment and case-based item bank must be built and reviewed before this course can become credential-bearing.
description: Develops multi-factor differential diagnosis across nutrient supply and uptake, root-zone moisture and chemistry, environmental gradients and loads, and crop-response patterns so learners can discriminate look-alike disorders using evidence rather than symptom labels alone.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate nutrient supply problems, uptake limitations, root-zone dysfunction, and environmental stressors using symptom distribution, chronology, root-zone measurements, crop history, and environmental evidence.
Evaluate pH, EC, moisture, drainage, media, root condition, and irrigation context as interacting evidence rather than treating any single measurement as a complete diagnosis.
Analyze spatial and temporal environmental patterns, airflow and load conditions, and sensor representativeness before assigning environmental contribution to a crop disorder.
Build ranked differentials for nutrient, root-zone, and environmental look-alikes and select the next measurement or observation most likely to change the ranking.
Document uncertainty, conflicting evidence, authorized next actions, and escalation triggers in a reconstructable specialist workup.
